html:
In 1889 Britain joined the small colony of Tobago to Trinidad, and in 1899 made it a ward of the larger island. The two have been one country since.

Tobago had been a rich sugar island in the late 1700s, fought over by the Courlanders, Dutch, French and British. After emancipation the sugar trade collapsed, and the island fell into debt and poverty.

Tobagonians long felt neglected by Port of Spain. Since 1980 the island has had its own House of Assembly. It is mostly Afro-Caribbean, while Trinidad has large Indian and African communities, and it lives largely from tourism.
